resolutions.title: The modified opacity contract is false of the existing parser API
resolutions.action: RE-WALKED 2026-09-18 and RESOLVED; supersedes the deferral recorded at 2026-09-17T21-30-50Z. The delta's requirement prose is rewritten to distinguish what the parser INTERPRETS (stage ids/titles, the two slot lines, section boundaries; docClass and violations derive from that grammar alone) from what it CARRIES (the document's raw lines as PASSTHROUGH, which confer no meaning and are the substrate section slicing is computed from). The engine readers that attach meaning to passthrough are now a CLOSED NAMED table with exactly two rows — sliceStageSection serving `orbit architecture show`, and orbit-source-lint's architecture.ruling-count — with any further reader required to be named there. The reader list was COUNTED, not assumed: every consumer of the parse was checked (validate.ts reads violations, buckets.ts reads stages, commands/architecture.ts is the command surface), and only those two touch doc.lines. One scenario added asserting that `show` reproduces charter prose verbatim while the parsed model is unchanged, which makes 'passthrough is passthrough' falsifiable rather than decorative. NO CODE CHANGED: ParsedArchitectureDoc keeps its shape, no consumer moved, 2197 tests green, the base fingerprint for this requirement re-verified, and all six original baseline scenarios are preserved byte-identically (the diff removes no scenario line).
resolutions.resolution: Repair, not redesign — 'apply the delta rewrite and re-walk the finding' (Sal, 2026-09-18), after a drafted replacement was reviewed in chat. The external offered two shapes and the earlier deferral costed the expensive one: separating raw bytes from the parsed model IS a code redesign that ripples to every consumer, but rewriting the requirement around semantic interpretation versus passthrough invents no mechanism — every sentence describes code that already exists and was read to write it — so R-crc-6 routes it nowhere. The deferral was also worse than it looked: this delta SYNCS INTO BASELINE at archive, so deferring would have written a known-false requirement into the live contract, defeating the very purpose the delta was added for two walks earlier.

resolutions.title: Escaped backticks incorrectly hide live markers
resolutions.action: computeCodeRegionMask now counts immediately-preceding backslashes and drops an escaped leading backtick from the candidate run. Reproduced first (a marker between two escaped backticks vanished). Regressions for odd and even backslash counts; the spec's inline-code table gained the row.

resolutions.title: An empty registry file disables the lint without any output
resolutions.action: `sources:` declaring no entries is now a SourceRegistryError naming the file and telling the author to delete it rather than empty it. Reproduced first (sources: {} yielded registryPresent true with zero findings, zero coverage, silent exit 0). The malformed-registry scenario gained the clause; the absent-file-silence test now covers present-but-null AND present-but-empty.

resolutions.title: Schema parameters can traverse outside the schema namespace
resolutions.action: findSchemaFile now requires the kebab SCHEMA_NAME_REGEX and enforces resolved-path containment within each tier (realpath, so symlinks cannot escape either). Reproduced first: `schema: ../../schemas/spec-driven` resolved a planted schema OUTSIDE both tiers and emitted 777. Regression covers four spellings; the spec states the identifier-not-path rule and gains a scenario.

resolutions.title: Tracked markdown read failures are silently reported as scanned
resolutions.action: A tracked path with no working-tree file is still skipped silently (a deleted file is legitimately still tracked), but every OTHER read failure is now a marker-kind finding naming the file, and filesScanned counts files actually READ. Three regressions: non-ASCII name, deleted file, unreadable file (chmod 000) with a stale sibling proving the rest still lints.

resolutions.title: Unmatched backtick runs cause repeated whole-suffix scans
resolutions.action: Pairing is now linear: each run's next equal-length partner is pre-indexed in one backward sweep, replacing the per-unmatched-run re-scan of the remaining group. Regression drives 400 unmatched runs of 17 distinct lengths under a time bound and still finds the live span.

Regression covers toString, constructor and hasOwnProperty, asserting the error lists the four exposed names.
